description: The figure illustrates several schematic bar-chart patterns intended to represent different distribution shapes used in a “parameter-efficient fine-tuning design space,” showing how values might be allocated across a sequence of components. In each mini chart, the categories are arranged along the horizontal axis as a left-to-right sequence of bars, but there are no explicit category names, axis titles, numeric tick marks, units, or visible scale markings; the vertical axis likewise has no label or numeric scale, so bar heights are only interpretable qualitatively. The first chart, labeled “Increasing,” contains four pale green bars with black outlines that rise from left to right, with the leftmost bar shortest and the rightmost bar tallest. The second chart, labeled “Uniform,” shows four pale green bars of approximately equal height. The third chart, labeled “Decreasing,” shows four pale green bars that step down from left to right, with the leftmost bar tallest and the rightmost bar shortest. The fourth chart (label not visible in the provided crop) shows four pale green bars with a low–high–high–low pattern, where the two middle bars are tallest and similar in height and the outer bars are shorter; a gray rectangular patch appears beneath this chart, partially obscuring where a label would be. The fifth chart, labeled “Bottleneck,” shows four pale green bars with a high–low–low–high pattern, where the first and last bars are taller and the two middle bars are shorter and similar. There is no legend, no stacking, and no grouped multi-series encoding; within each mini chart the bars appear ordered by position to depict the named pattern rather than being sorted by a numeric axis, and no individual bars are specially emphasized beyond the consistent outline and fill style.
